scope: Prepared local patch; not committed or deployed. Audit status remains open until its owning scope is verified.

findings.title: Users can grant themselves administrator roles
Profile policies expose and permit modification of other users’ data
Wallet owners can directly edit their balance
Reward tables have unrestricted “service role” policies
Hospital data isolation is missing from supplied policies and incomplete in fix scripts
Clinical interpretation functions bypass patient assignment checks
Messaging proxies accept untrusted callers, including bot webhook changes
findings.preparedChange: Five optional messaging/AI Netlify endpoints deny every request in prepared source. Supabase messaging endpoints and existing deployments are unchanged.

findings.title: Incoming messaging webhooks do not verify provider authenticity
findings.preparedChange: Prepared Netlify webhook entrypoints are non-operational. Provider authenticity work and Supabase webhook verification remain pending.

findings.title: Several privileged functions lack application-level caller authorization
Database HTML and printable records are rendered without sanitization
Posture-photo setup makes medical images publicly accessible
HMS access is a broad frontend gate, not module-level enforcement
Doctor self-update protection omits newer permission fields
Session changes do not invalidate all role and query caches
Repository contains reusable test credentials and production-oriented test instructions
Legacy browser integrations still expect private API keys
findings.preparedChange: Unsafe browser-prefixed Telegram token removed from the environment example. Legacy browser service helpers remain dormant and unrepaired.

findings.title: AI endpoints have weak cost, payload and feature controls
Audit logs are client-authored and best-effort
Custom login throttling is bypassable and lacks committed server implementations
Prices and free-payment states are chosen by the browser
Valid payment signatures can be replayed against a different internal purchase
Successful shop payment writes an order status rejected by the supplied schema
Payment completion depends on a browser callback with no committed reconciliation handler
Refunds can be marked complete without returning money
Payout processing is not atomic or protected against concurrent processing
Billing creates paid invoices regardless of actual payment mode
Goods receipts can lose stock updates and prematurely close purchase orders
Pharmacy sales do not implement the promised invoice and stock operation
Coupons and checkout retries are not a coherent persisted transaction
Therapy settlement can record settled after partial or failed credits
Empty patient histories are replaced by fabricated allergies and conditions
Document parsing invents medical values instead of reading the uploaded document
Some AI risk, vital and posture results are fixed demonstrations presented as personal findings
Spine therapy records are attached to the logged-in clinician as the patient
Admission and bed occupancy are separate, unchecked writes
Prescription creation and dispensing can leave contradictory records
Consultation code confuses doctor profile IDs with authentication IDs
Teleconsultation links point to an incompatible record identifier
Lab orders have zero pricing and lose legitimate numeric zero results
Medical signing is not bound to an assigned case or an atomic signed record
Offline clinical operations can be dropped, duplicated or synchronized under another session
Consent management reports grants/revocations without implementing them
ABHA/ABDM linking is a stub even when credentials are configured
Health Locker shows fabricated records and claims actions that do not occur
Duplicate-patient merge does not merge or dismiss any records
Security Controls settings do not save or enforce the advertised protections
Some booking hooks report success when persistence fails
International booking and device connection features are local demonstrations
Developer MCP and voice agent features simulate execution
Paid membership activates directly and expired memberships still pass gates
Paid digital products expose their file location before purchase
Coin redemption trusts cached balances and client-supplied redemption amounts
Doctor-only feed visibility is not enforced in database reads
Feed poll UI has no voting workflow and conflicts with schema
Quiz answers and scoring are client-controlled
Quiz daily selection and streak progression do not implement their stated rules
User-type onboarding routes distinct roles into doctor registration
Advertised typecheck command does not check application files
findings.preparedChange: Application and config projects are targeted explicitly; a real compiler fixture proves the former empty-root false green. Full repository type debt remains unverified.

findings.title: Unused payment helper has a syntax error hidden from the production build
findings.preparedChange: Nested documentation comment repaired; changed file passes parser verification.

findings.title: Database setup is split between migrations and hundreds of manual-script dependencies
Migration history contains duplicate version prefixes and unsafe setup scripts
Client calls backend functions that are absent from the repository
Type safety is bypassed on a large scale and lint cannot act as a release gate
Entity switching crashes because its provider is never mounted
Branch context is unmounted and cannot define a reliable tenant boundary
An unused booking helper calls React hooks from an ordinary async function
findings.preparedChange: Dormant booking utility accepts injected services and no longer calls hooks; persistence/notification failure paths are tested.

findings.title: Role definitions and patient/appointment models are fragmented
Task tracking has competing stores, silent fallback and missing role scoping
Appointment preparation listens to a field not defined by the booking schema
Public provider views inherit restrictions that can empty the directory
Configured browser headers block integrations used by the code
Netlify handlers mix CommonJS with an ES-module package
findings.preparedChange: Five deployed Netlify entrypoints are now dependency-free ESM preview responders; native imports pass. Hosted bundling is deferred.

findings.title: Delivery and notification integrations claim success without their external action
findings.preparedChange: Exposed WhatsApp fake-success behavior is replaced by a 503 preview response. Courier/Supabase implementations are unchanged.

findings.title: Current tests and CI cannot establish portal correctness
findings.preparedChange: Automatic source-check workflow prepared. It has not run on GitHub; database and browser journey checks remain pending.

findings.title: Locked dependencies have current vulnerability advisories
Bundle structure and global UI create avoidable loading overhead
SEO prerendering is disconnected from the default deploy and crawler rules conflict
Admin layout and several interactive controls need accessibility/mobile work
Historical reports and setup documents are not reliable evidence of current readiness
